candidates.name: Optic Nerve Glioma
support_spans: Focal enhancement along enlarged right optic nerve
Diffuse enlargement of orbital portion of right optic nerve, enhancement of nerve sheath
candidates.why: The patient's presentation with sudden vision loss and optic disc swelling, combined with imaging findings of an enlarged optic nerve and enhancement on MRI, suggests an optic nerve glioma.
candidates.protected_reason: This diagnosis may be easily missed due to its rarity and the patient's complex medical history, including treatment with immunosuppressive agents.

candidates.name: Retinal Artery Occlusion
support_spans: Occlusion of the superior branch artery
Combined occlusion of the central retinal artery and vein
candidates.why: The patient's sudden vision loss and findings of retinal artery occlusion on examination and fluorescein angiography support this diagnosis.
candidates.protected_reason: This diagnosis may be overlooked due to the patient's underlying treatment with bevacizumab, which can increase the risk of thrombotic events.

candidates.protected_reason: This diagnosis may be challenging to establish due to the rarity of vitreoretinal lymphoma and the need for histopathological confirmation.
